handback.t:
R5-A (H9, warm-start priors) is finished. Verdict: keep one candidate, `pop-guard+conf`, as an opt-in conditional lever, not a default. All numbers are synthetic until validated on real traffic. I made no src edits and no commits.

**What survives.** `pop-guard+conf` is the recommended guarded-safe router with its per-(feature, agent) counts seeded from a pool of K previous deployments' logged outcomes. Each prior carries a per-feature trust weight learned online, so a wrong prior is overridden within a handful of outcomes. When the keyword rule is abandoned or absent, the router follows the best pool-informed agent instead of asking the cold learner.
- With an empty prior it is bit-identical to `recommended_router`; this self-check runs at the start of every `h9_priors` run.
- Pool setup: K=6 previous deployments, 1000 tasks each, logged by the default router.
- Tuned on seeds 1-8 on 7 of the 14 worlds. The other 7 are never seen by the tuner: sim-NoTraps, sim-mismatch, big pool, shift, held-out family, no-info and uninformative-feedback.
- Run on held 31-60 and on fresh blocks 61-90 and 91-120 with the same frozen tuning.

**Worlds.**
- Generator A reuses `sim::World` and the f3 `BigWorld`.
- Generator B is my own multi-domain world with agency, 20-agent and latent-factor pools.
- 14 worlds in total: related-pool treatment worlds, a pool-distribution-shift world, a held-out family, a wrong-prior world, a no-prior-info world, a randomized world, an equal-agents control and an uninformative-feedback control.

**Gains (vs best fair baseline).** Early-horizon gains are Holm-significant in two independent worlds, from two different generators, on all three blocks.

| World | H50 | H100 | H250 | H500 | H2000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 sim-Fixed, pool = same hidden skills | +0.081 to +0.092 | +0.074 to +0.087 | +0.056 to +0.065 | +0.037 to +0.041 | about +0.01 (raw only) |
| B1 multi-domain, 10% of domains re-drawn | +0.013 to +0.020 | +0.015 to +0.020 | +0.015 to +0.021 | +0.012 to +0.016 | +0.003 to +0.008 |

- A1 reaches 95% of oracle 117-157 tasks sooner.
- B1 is a Holm win at H250 on all three blocks; at H50 it is a Holm win on two blocks and raw-only on the third.
- No Holm losses in treatment worlds.
- B2 (40% re-drawn) and the big pool give +0.002 to +0.009, mostly not Holm-significant.
- The effect fades by ~2000 as expected. In A1 the 1000-2000 window is -0.013 vs the best baseline (Holm-significant on 31-60 and 61-90, not on 91-120).

**Wrong prior (A5 sim-mismatch, B6 specialists all moved).** The cost is bounded and recovers. The worst mean loss over both worlds, per block:

| Horizon | Worst mean loss |
|---|---|
| H50 | -0.031, -0.0205, -0.0165 (worst CI lower bound -0.046) |
| H100 | -0.019 or better |
| H250 | -0.007 or better |
| H2000 | -0.002 |

- The trust weight makes this 2-3x smaller than without it (`pop-guard`: -0.035 to -0.051 at H50).
- My informal "no more than 0.02 at any H" bound is not met at H50 on one block. I did not pre-register the bound, so I report the numbers and do not call it pass/fail.

**Controls.**
- Randomized, no-traps, big-32 and equal-agents worlds: |diff| of at most about 0.003, and exactly 0 for equal-agents (no Holm losses).
- No-prior-info world: -0.007 to -0.010 at H50, with one Holm loss at H100 on 91-120.
- Held-out family: raw loss of at most 0.004.
- TOST ±0.01 shows Holm equivalence in 19, 20 and 23 of 25 control cells.
- Uninformative feedback hurts every learner against the static keyword map, so it is not the prior's fault. Against its cold counterpart `pop-guard+conf` is +0.002 to +0.005 early.
- Pool-shift world: the early gain does not reproduce across blocks (+0.021, +0.010, +0.006) and the late window is -0.002 to -0.022. Do not rely on it under drift plus unknown agents.

**Dead or negative results.**
- `pop-ts+conf` (Thompson with a pool prior) gains +0.03 to +0.12 over cold pooled-ts at H50 but sits 0.10-0.36 below the best baseline.
- `pop-map` (pool-corrected keyword map) is best in A1 and the shift world at H50 but loses -0.16 to -0.25 in the wrong-prior and no-info worlds (A5, B6, B8).
- `kw-cal` (pool-calibrated keyword-prior strength) ties everything.
- The hierarchical-shrinkage ablation is within ±0.001 of plain pooled counts, so shrinkage is not what makes it work. Coverage rule, trust weight and informed fallback are.
- K=1 gives no effect; the effect saturates around K=4.
- Cost is about 3.3 µs/task vs 1.7 for guarded-safe (unoptimised, shared box), and 2x state per feature row.

**Disclosures (full list in the board entry).**
- I redesigned after seeing quick 31-60 runs, so 31-60 is not clean held-out; conclusions rest on 61-90 and 91-120.
- The uninformative-feedback control was added after seeing 31-60 results.
- Pool logs are selection-biased by the logging router; the coverage rule is a heuristic fix.
- The tasks-to-target definition changed once before the final runs.
- Best baseline per world and metric is picked post hoc, which favours the baselines.
- A rerun of 61-90 reproduced the logged results exactly. I did not run `cargo test --lib`; no library change.
